answer: One applicant registers a vine bridge across one river bend for 120 days. The applicant weaves 40 vine strands, ties a pearl marker to each anchor post, and logs every crossing signed by a neighbor. An inspector crosses it twice, checking the log against footprints. A forged log forfeits a 150 token deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Forging 10,000 bridges freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A vine bridge holds because each strand was twisted by hand, like a pearl growing around one grain of sand; the fake one snaps under the first traveler and the deposit is gone.
